newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent steady as Iraq counters strong gasoline.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent steady as Iraq counters strong gasoline.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures were little changed on Wednesday afternoon with expectations of heavy flows of Iraqi crude in August scrambling bullish signals from a tight U.S. gasoline market.

August Brent, which expires at the close of business on Wednesday, was trading two cents down at $18.37 a barrel at 1430 GMT. The front month contract was trading at parity to September which was steady on Tuesday's close.
Iraqi exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal could reach 1.5 million barrels per day in August, with virtually all of this quarter's $1-billion of sales concentrated in that month.

Western diplomats at the United Nations said on Tuesday that Iraq would be allowed to carry over only five percent of its sales in the current 90 day sales period, which started on June 8, to the next quarter.
This would mean Iraq, having delayed the restart of exports for two months, will have to sell oil at a much higher rate in August than previously expected, or forego some of its sales.
Exports in the first six-month term of the scheme averaged around 660,000 bpd.
But weekly stocks figures from the U.S. showing a fairly sharp drawdown on gasoline were stemming sharper losses, brokers said.
"The market sentiment is for crude to go lower, but prompt gasoline in the States is pretty tight and at the front end gasoline cracks have widened out a lot recently," said one dealer.
Data from the U.S. Department of Energy indicated a 3.9 million barrels draw on gasoline stocks last week.
Strength at the front end of the market was helping to narrow the contango on the front Brent spread, brokers said.
"At the moment the North Sea crude looks fairly stable but there is a feeling that with Iraq pumping quite a bit come September the market will be well-supplied," said one.
August gas oil was trading 75 cents up at $163.50 a tonne at 1455 GMT.
